question: A 76-year-old man presents for a follow-up appointment at his primary care provider’s office. The patient has severe osteoarthritis, which substantially limits his daily physical activity. Several imaging studies have confirmed severe articular degeneration and evidence of bone grinding on bone in his hip joints. The patient suffers from chronic pain and depression that have been resistant to medication. At the physician’s office, his blood pressure is 119/67 mm Hg, the respirations are 18/min, the pulse is 87/min, and the temperature is 36.7°C (98.0°F). On physical examination, the patient has a flat affect and appears anxious. He has significant pain and limited passive and active range of motion of his hip joints bilaterally. This patient would most likely benefit from which of the following procedures if there are no contraindications?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Severe osteoarthritis with limited physical activity -> chronic pain and depression -> resistant to medication -> limited range of motion in hip joints -> significant pain and functional impairment -> potential need for surgical intervention -> Total hip arthroplasty -> 85%

CHAIN: Severe articular degeneration and bone grinding on bone in hip joints -> significant joint damage -> conservative management ineffective -> consideration for surgical intervention -> Total hip arthroplasty -> 80%
CHAIN: Chronic pain and depression -> decreased quality of life -> limited physical activity -> hip joint degeneration -> surgical intervention may be necessary -> Total hip arthroplasty -> 75%
analysis: Given the severe articular degeneration and chronic pain in the hip joints of the 76-year-old man, along with limited physical activity and resistance to medication for pain and depression, the most appropriate procedure would be Total Hip Arthroplasty (THA) to relieve pain, improve function, and enhance quality of life.
